entries.title: Memory chip shortages prompt companies worldwide to set up procurement war rooms; some chip prices have risen 10x in a year, driving up electronics prices (Wall Street Journal)
Analysis: the S&P 500 software and semiconductor subindices are both slightly down YTD, with software outperforming semiconductors as the AI narrative shifts (Emily Herbert/Financial Times)
Microsoft says state-backed hacking groups in China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added AI penetration testing tool ARTEX to their arsenals (Jonathan Greig/The Record)
Sources: Nvidia tells its manufacturing partners to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia as the US steps up export controls (Financial Times)
Sensor Tower: Shein's app averaged ~6M MAUs in India in October, flat since January, vs. market leader Myntra's 100M; Reliance oversees Shein's India operations (Bloomberg)
Letter: Leopold Aschenbrenner told investors Situational Awareness lost 65% after fees in Q3; the fund is up 88.5% after fees for the year through September (Wall Street Journal)
Sources: Trump's national security adviser, Secretary Marco Rubio, was not involved in efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang and expressed anger at his return (Jo Ling/CBS News)
OpenAI rolls out its merged ChatGPT Chat and Work tabs, with a shared usage meter, to a small group of Pro users, saying heavy users may hit their limits sooner (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
Investigation: Nvidia sells its most advanced chips to at least two Chinese-owned California companies, which have leased or sold some of them to firms in Asia (Josh Boswell/CBS News)
Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
Neuralink says it got FDA approval for the LINK Pivotal Study, a US clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of its BCI system in ALS patients (Craig Trudell/Bloomberg)
A US court dismisses Amazon's challenge to a 2025 CPSC order requiring it to recall 400K+ hazardous products sold by third parties via Fulfillment by Amazon (Emma Roth/The Verge)
A coalition of 42 AGs opposes Character.AI's plan to auction off data from 21M+ US accounts, 2.1M+ registered to minors, saying the sale lacks user protections (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
Hands-on with the "Install as app" feature for Claude artifacts: they are HTML apps wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is managed via the main Claude app (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
Sources: Pete Hegseth and other Pentagon officials discussed using the Defense Production Act as leverage to pressure Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang (Washington Post)
